output.summary: The deterministic verdict is preserved: run validity VALID, analysis coverage COMPLETE, and policy_verdict NO_POLICY — no SLO was configured, so no PASS/FAIL assessment was produced; NO_POLICY is not a pass. The run was executed at a constant target of 20 requests/s (min=max=mean=median=20, sample_standard_deviation 0 in both windows). Overall the analysis shows 7200 samples, error_count 0, and latency p50/p95/p99 ≈ 203/236/239 ms (window p50: 201 ms reference vs 204 ms evaluation). Sixteen resource-vs-p95-latency correlation pairs were tested; 15 were BELOW_EFFECT and 4 were CANDIDATE, but only pair-14 (resource-14) was SELECTED by the Holm-adjusted bootstrap (holm_adjusted_p_value 0.016, max_p_value 0.001; best_lag_rho -0.487172887046 at best_lag_ms -10000; uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED). The best lag sits at the boundary of the scanned range and clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag or causal interpretation is supported. The diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested 0 and episodes_reported 0, which does not prove stability.

hypotheses.observation: Headline selection SELECTED pair-14 (resource-14 vs p95 latency) with holm_adjusted_p_value 0.016, max_p_value 0.001, status SELECTED; the pair record shows status CANDIDATE, best_lag_ms -10000 (edge of the scanned -10000..10000 range), best_lag_rho -0.487172887046, partial_rho -0.105232474746, raw_rho -0.105232474746, and uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; the correlation-candidate finding references this pair.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: There may be a genuine negative association between resource-14 ratio and p95 latency, but the peak occurring at the boundary of the scanned lags, the unverified clock relationship, and the small difference between window latency aggregates (reference p50 201 ms vs evaluation p50 204 ms) make it plausible this is a truncated or aliased correlation rather than a proven time-shifted causal effect.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment/synchronization first, then rerun the correlation with lags extending beyond ±10000 ms and a longer evaluation window, inspecting the raw resource-14 series and adding uncertainty/confidence estimation since uncertainty is currently NOT_ESTIMATED.

hypotheses.observation: Pairs pair-04, pair-11, and pair-12 have status CANDIDATE with best_lag_rho values -0.342830910072, -0.322225144351, and 0.330827674706 respectively; their unadjusted max_p_value values are 0.049, 0.054, and 0.034, but Holm-adjusted p-values are 0.686, 0.702, and 0.51, so none was SELECTED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: These near-threshold correlations could be family-wise noise across the 16 hypothesis tests, or they could reflect one shared driver that moves several resource series together; none of them demonstrates a proven effect on p95 latency.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Plot resource-04, resource-11, and resource-12 together with p95 latency, check for a common pattern or shared host effect, and run confirmatory tests with more data or a reduced hypothesis family.

hypotheses.observation: The target load series is constant at 20 requests/s in both windows (min=max=mean=median=20, sample_standard_deviation 0), and every correlation pair lists reasons CONSTANT_CONTROL with controls_requested ['target'] but controls_used [].
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because load did not vary, its influence on latency cannot be estimated or controlled; observed correlations between resource ratios and latency could instead reflect internal scheduling, co-located workloads, or noise rather than load-driven effects.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with stepped or randomized request rates so the target is non-constant and usable as a control, and capture co-located workload/process data for the service host.

hypotheses.observation: Both window policy summaries (reference and evaluation) report verdict NO_POLICY with business_verdict NO_POLICY and resource_verdict NO_POLICY, and the analysis policy_verdict is NO_POLICY even though run validity is VALID and coverage is COMPLETE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: No SLO/policy was configured, so the pipeline could not assess compliance; NO_POLICY should not be interpreted as proof that the service met any performance or resource target.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Introduce explicit policies (e.g., latency percentile thresholds, error-rate caps, resource utilization limits) with defined evaluation windows and rerun so outputs can be PASS/FAIL.

caveats: policy_verdict is NO_POLICY; a missing policy is not a pass, and no PASS/FAIL statement exists in this analysis.
